points.description: States that the compiler (not the programmer) automatically provides/creates a default constructor when no constructor is defined/provided for the class.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if it says a default constructor is created automatically by the compiler but does not clearly state the condition that no constructor is provided.

points.description: States that if any constructor is defined for the class (e.g. a parameterized constructor), the compiler does NOT create a default constructor.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if it only implies this (e.g. 'only when no constructor exists') without explicitly stating that defining any constructor suppresses the implicit default constructor.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both facts stated precisely: the compiler supplies a default constructor when the class has no constructor, and it does not when any constructor is user-defined. Part marks only when clearly more than half of a point is stated. Vague statements, wrong claims (e.g. compiler always creates one, or the programmer creates it), or talk about unrelated constructor types earn nothing for that point.
